verdict.rationale: Superset can clone a remote repo, create isolated worktree workspaces (including programmatically via MCP), and run user-defined setup scripts that install dependencies and transfer env variables. However, these are user-configured provisioning steps, not an agent autonomously setting up its own environment, and the setup-script capability is evidenced only by a founder comment rather than first-party docs. Missing for 10: first-party docs for setup scripts, evidence of agent-driven (rather than user-defined) environment configuration, evidence that cloning is automated rather than done through a dialog, and hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can have an agent automatically clone the repo, install dependencies, and configure its own working environment

citations.quote: superset manages worktrees + runs setup/teardown scripts you define on project setup. Those scripts can install dependencies, transfer env variables, and spin up branching services.
Add your repo from a local folder or clone a remote repository.
create Git-worktree workspaces, launch coding-agent sessions
Each agent gets an isolated Git worktree and its own branch.
